question: In advanced COPD, hypercapnia (elevated PaCO₂) develops primarily because the patient breathes in too little oxygen, not because of reduced alveolar ventilation.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. Hypercapnia reflects inadequate alveolar ventilation relative to CO₂ production — caused by V/Q mismatch, increased dead space ventilation, and fatigued respiratory muscles — not a deficiency of inspired O₂.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. Hypercapnia in COPD results from alveolar hypoventilation due to V/Q mismatch, increased dead space, and respiratory muscle fatigue. It is not caused by a low inspired oxygen fraction.
